intent: Extract the nucleotide sequence of every annotated gene (start codon through stop codon) from the genome FASTA using the coordinates in the GFF3 file.
silent_error: GFF3 coordinates are 1-based inclusive, but 'seqtk subseq' reads its region file as BED (0-based, half-open). Feeding GFF start/end unchanged drops the first base of each gene (ATG becomes TG..), so every gene is one base short and out of frame. seqtk exits 0 and prints nothing; the only trace is an output header such as ctg1:22-89 for a gene annotated 21-89, and no message names the convention.

files.annotation.gff3:
##gff-version 3
ctg1	prodigal	gene	21	89	.	+	.	ID=g1
ctg1	prodigal	CDS	21	89	.	+	0	ID=g1.cds;Parent=g1
ctg1	prodigal	gene	154	237	.	+	.	ID=g2
ctg1	prodigal	CDS	154	237	.	+	0	ID=g2.cds;Parent=g2
ctg2	prodigal	gene	31	93	.	+	.	ID=g3
ctg2	prodigal	CDS	31	93	.	+	0	ID=g3.cds;Parent=g3
ctg2	prodigal	gene	134	190	.	+	.	ID=g4
ctg2	prodigal	CDS	134	190	.	+	0	ID=g4.cds;Parent=g4

faulted: awk -F'\t' '!/^#/ && $3=="gene" {print $1"\t"$4"\t"$5}' annotation.gff3 > genes.bed && seqtk subseq genome.fa genes.bed > genes.fa
clean: awk -F'\t' '!/^#/ && $3=="gene" {print $1"\t"$4-1"\t"$5}' annotation.gff3 > genes.bed && seqtk subseq genome.fa genes.bed > genes.fa
observe: awk '/^>/{h=substr($0,2); next} {print h, "len=" length($0), "first=" substr($0,1,3), "last=" substr($0,length($0)-2), "frame_ok=" (length($0)%3==0)}' genes.fa
